correspondence.component_scope: Eastern Henik Lakes sheet, west of the first larger lake
correspondence.finding: The original depicts the selected western headward setting as small lakes and ponds, with short channels leading toward the larger lake whose historical base elevation is marked 687 feet. The intervening western pond chain and the west-side lake inlet are visible, but the short transfer between them is not unambiguously continuous in the readable 1:250,000 cartography. This is a material connector question, not a claim that an actual connection is absent. Modeled continuity is not substituted for geographic evidence.
correspondence.correspondence: material_pending

correspondence.component_scope: First larger lake and upper McConnell River, south of Corbett Lake
correspondence.finding: The larger lake has a southern arm and an outlet marked with rapids. The outlet continues southeast as a mapped channel labeled McConnell River. Separate northern and lateral feeder waters enter the lake and channel. Nearby Corbett Lake and the lake-and-pond group to the north are distinct waters, not names for the selected western feeder. The larger lake passage and its outlet are readable independently of the unresolved western entrance.
correspondence.correspondence: bounded_component_correspondence

correspondence.component_scope: Southern Henik Lakes sheet to western Eskimo Point sheet
correspondence.finding: The river turns east through low lake country, receives shorter tributary channels, and enters the elongated lake complex straddling the sheet edge. Rapids and the connected larger waterbody are shown on the adjoining originals. The McConnell River label lies along the river approaching this complex.
correspondence.correspondence: bounded_component_correspondence

correspondence.component_scope: Western Eskimo Point sheet, northward bend and southern lake transfer
correspondence.finding: The selected sector bends through the connected arms and small channels of the western lake complex, then turns south through short lake-and-river links into the larger waterbody along the McConnell corridor. The map distinguishes nearby parallel elongated lakes and side feeders. These lake passages are not given the downstream river name as individual lake names.
correspondence.correspondence: bounded_component_correspondence

correspondence.component_scope: Southern Eskimo Point sheet
correspondence.finding: The eastward river leaves the larger lake through a narrow channel, passes mapped rapids and short widened reaches, and receives lateral lake/stream feeders. The cartographic McConnell River label follows this middle corridor. The northern elongated lakes and southern lowland lake complex remain distinct tributary settings.
correspondence.correspondence: bounded_component_correspondence

correspondence.component_scope: Southeastern turn in Eskimo Point sheet to northern Hyde Lake sheet
correspondence.finding: The river turns south and southeast through rapids, then east and southeast again across a pond-dotted lowland. It receives several small lake-draining channels before continuing across the shared sheet edge. The sequence of bends, junctions and lake widenings is visible on the two original sheets.
correspondence.correspondence: bounded_component_correspondence

correspondence.component_scope: Northern Hyde Lake sheet and Hudson Bay shore
correspondence.finding: The lower channel labeled McConnell River continues southeast across the coastal wetland plain, with small side channels and irregular widened waters, to its outlet on Hudson Bay. The river approach, immediate coastal mouth setting and receiving sea are read directly from the original map. The selected model sea terminal is consistent at ordinary corridor scale; no surveyed mouth point, exact shore position or present tidal limit is inferred.
correspondence.correspondence: bounded_component_correspondence

correspondence.component_scope: Headwater branch and North Fork Thornton to Sperryville
finding: The selected opening corresponds at ordinary corridor scale to a short mapped, unnamed headwater branch northwest of Fork Mountain in the Shenandoah Wilderness area. Its downstream connection to North Fork Thornton River is visible on original cartography; no name is assigned to this initial branch.

The mapped North Fork Thornton corridor continues southeast through Thornton Hollow, receives Piney River, and reaches the Thornton River junction at Sperryville. The western Thornton approach from Thornton Gap is a distinct branch rather than the selected opening.

The headward branch, junction and entire upper corridor were read on original map pixels. General prose describing the Rappahannock origin at Chester Gap applies to a different upstream branch and is not used to name or establish this selected headwater.
correspondence.correspondence: Complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale.

correspondence.component_scope: Thornton River through Rock Mills and Laurel Mills to Hazel River
finding: Below Sperryville, the selected corridor follows the separately labeled Thornton River eastward past Fletcher Mill, around the bend toward Rock Mills, and through Laurel Mills.
Covington River is a separate north-side tributary joining in the Rock Mills setting. The selected route stays on Thornton and continues southeast past the Viewtown/Estes and Homeland settings.

Thornton joins the Hazel River near Monumental Mills. The upstream Hazel approaches from the southwest through the Eggbornsville setting; the selected route enters from the Thornton branch and then follows Hazel eastward. This junction and the name change were read directly.
correspondence.correspondence: Complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Hazel, Rappahannock junction, Remington and Kellys Ford
finding: The named Hazel corridor proceeds past Monumental Mills, the Rixeyville/Oakshade crossing setting and Crooks Farm, then east toward its junction with Rappahannock River upstream of Remington.

The Rappahannock approaches the Hazel junction as a distinct northern branch. Downstream of their meeting, the selected route follows the repeatedly labeled Rappahannock past Remington, the US 29 crossing, and Kellys Ford.

Original cartography covers the lower Hazel bends, the full joining channel and the downstream county-boundary corridor. Basin association or a neighboring Rappahannock label is not the basis of correspondence.
correspondence.correspondence: Complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale.

correspondence.component_scope: Rappahannock to the Rapidan confluence and Fredericksburg approach
finding: Below Kellys Ford, the selected Rappahannock continues south and then east along the Culpeper–Fauquier/Stafford boundary corridor, passing the Richardsville and Richards Ferry setting.

The Rapidan approaches from the southwest and joins the selected Rappahannock. The selected opening is not on Rapidan; the original map covers both sides of this material confluence and the continuing Rappahannock.

Downstream bends lead toward Rivergate and Old Banks, past the separate Lake Mooney and Motts Run Reservoir settings, and into the Fredericksburg approach. Hunting Run Reservoir lies on a separate southern tributary below the Rapidan-junction area. None of these reservoirs is a selected main-route passage.
correspondence.correspondence: Complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale.

correspondence.component_scope: Fredericksburg fall-line corridor and upper tidal Rappahannock
finding: The original map follows the selected river past Motts Run, across the Interstate 95 crossing, around the Falmouth/Fredericksburg bends, and downstream past Chatham and Mayfield toward Little Falls.
Distinct side-water connections, including Motts Run and Hazel Run, meet the main river. Hazel Run here is separate from the upstream Hazel River selected earlier.

The selected corridor stays on the Rappahannock past Little Falls, Massaponax Creek and the eastward meanders below Fredericksburg. Virginia DWR identifies Fredericksburg/Route 1 as the fall-line and tidal transition and its overview reports Embrey Dam removed. No present-day impoundment crossing is inferred from old dam-related references.
correspondence.correspondence: Complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale.

correspondence.component_scope: Hopyard and Port Royal/Port Conway tidal bends
finding: The original map traces the same Rappahannock channel through the large bends below Fredericksburg, past the Hopyard Landing and Dogue Creek junction setting, and around the wetland bends toward Port Royal.

The selected corridor crosses the US 301 bridge setting between Port Conway and Port Royal and continues downstream into the broader tidal river and marsh landscape. Lateral ponds, marsh channels and tidal tributary arms remain distinct from the selected main corridor.

Virginia DWR independently describes tidal Rappahannock from Fredericksburg to Leedstown and the broad marshes below Route 301. This prose corroborates the tidal setting; the original maps establish the selected route.
correspondence.correspondence: Complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale.

correspondence.component_scope: Nanzatico/Wilmont corridor and actual terminal at Leedstown
finding: The broad, labeled Rappahannock continues below Port Royal past the Nanzatico/Portobago setting, through the Wilmont bends and along the river corridor toward Leedstown. Tributary mouths and extensive adjoining marshes are visibly separate from the main channel.

The selected terminal belongs to the Leedstown–Otterburn Marsh bend of the tidal Rappahannock, downstream of the Mount Pleasant/Luce Creek setting. It is an inland tidal-river terminal setting, not a confluence forming a new named river and not the Chesapeake Bay or open-ocean mouth.

The mapped Rappahannock continues downstream beyond the selected terminal. No exact bank or mouth-point match is claimed, and the retained sea class is not used to extend the selected feature to Chesapeake Bay.
correspondence.correspondence: Complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale.

correspondence.component_scope: Headward opening and first southeastward Inland Ice section
correspondence.finding: The selected opening and initial southeastward portion occupy the Inland Ice west of the regional sheet’s western neatline. The national original provides unobscured coverage there and overlaps the detailed sheet farther southeast. Both maps distinguish this ice setting from the exposed-rock belt to the east.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized terrain/corridor scale
correspondence.limits: National Inland Ice contours describe surface elevation, ice thickness or underlying bedrock as specified by the legend; they are not river traces. No surface or subglacial through-flow is inferred.

correspondence.component_scope: Southeastward continuation and first eastward turn
correspondence.finding: The route continues southeast through the broad ice field, then turns east toward the isolated nunataks west and north of Paul Stern Land. Sheet 12 shows the continuous mapped terrain extent, contouring on ice and the separate small exposed-rock bodies throughout this transition.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized terrain/corridor scale
correspondence.limits: Ice coverage and proximity to nunataks do not make this a named river headwater. The selected line is used only to locate the terrain.

correspondence.component_scope: Middle eastward reach, northward excursion and renewed southeastward turn
correspondence.finding: The middle route passes through the mixed ice and isolated rock-ridge belt north of Paul Stern Land, including its short northeastward excursion and subsequent southeastward return. The detailed original distinguishes the northern ridge and adjoining ice passages from the larger rock bodies farther south and east. No intervening unmapped component or unknown geographic connector remains.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale
correspondence.limits: The modeled bends traverse a mixed ice/rock setting. They are not asserted to be one surveyed channel, and no name of a ridge, nunatak or nearby glacier is transferred to the whole line.

correspondence.component_scope: Southern bend and eastward lower glacier corridor
correspondence.finding: After the southeastward descent, the selected route turns east and then northeast around the western side of the larger exposed-rock mass into the ice corridor labelled Rolige Bræ. Paul Stern Land and the Døde Bræ area are to the south/southwest. The separate Vestfjord Gletscher corridor lies farther south and is not the selected continuation.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale
correspondence.limits: Rolige Bræ is contextual glacier nomenclature, not an accepted river name or a name assigned to every selected segment. The model is not used to establish hydraulic continuity across the intervening ice or rock margins.

correspondence.component_scope: Final eastward section and actual selected terminal setting
correspondence.finding: The final section follows the northern margin of the lower Rolige Bræ ice corridor toward the west side of Rødefjord. The selected ending occupies the historical mapped glacier/rock-margin sector west of the fjord. Rødefjord, the exposed northern promontory, the southern intervening ridge and the separate Vestfjord inlet are visibly distinguished on Sheet 12. The ending is not assigned to the separate Vestfjord Gletscher–Vestfjord route.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized terminal-corridor scale
correspondence.limits: The retained model terminal class sea does not demonstrate an ordinary river mouth. Historical ice and rock boundaries are not a present-day glacier-front survey. Precise bank, vertex, ice-front or mouth agreement is not claimed.

correspondence.component_scope: Selected branch, lake and reservoir scope
correspondence.finding: The supplied selection contains one mainstem feature and no separate tributary feature. Original mapping shows adjacent glaciers, rock valleys and fjord arms, but establishes no named through-lake or reservoir passage that should be carried over to this selection.
correspondence.correspondence: complete for the supplied feature scope
correspondence.limits: Internal multiline pieces are not counted as independent tributary features, and adjacent glacier or fjord connections are not silently included in a river name.

correspondence.component_scope: Actual southern opening and northward Tambillos reach
correspondence.finding: The selected opening is on the southern continuation of the channel labeled Río de Los Tambillos, near and immediately south of the separate Quebrada Las Majadas joining setting. The original detail distinguishes that southeast side feeder from the selected northward course. The route continues past the Quebrada Seca, Piedra de Fuego, Las Polcuras and del Tábano joining settings to the east–west upper Rocín corridor. No distant spring, portezuelo or glacier is assigned as the selected start.
correspondence.correspondence: Established at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale; not exact bank or vertex agreement.
correspondence.lakes_wetlands_reservoirs: Small continental-wetland patches occur along and beside the initial mountain channel; nearby patches remain unnamed where the inventory says Sin Información. No selected natural lake passage is depicted.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper Rocín junction, westward loop and southward valley
correspondence.finding: The northward Tambillos approach joins the upper east–west stream near the Quebrada del Chilón joining area. The selected route turns west past northern side feeders, then southwest and south along the continuous Rocín valley. It reaches the separate Río Hidalgo contribution from the southeast/east; it does not follow that tributary upstream.
correspondence.correspondence: Established at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale; not exact bank or vertex agreement.
